Account and Login Help > Password and Login Issues
### How do I reset my password?
1. Go to dashboard.stratifylabs.io and click "Sign In"
2. Click "Forgot password?" below the login form
3. Enter the email address associated with your account
4. Check your inbox for a password reset link — it arrives within a few minutes
5. Click the link and set a new password

The reset link expires after 1 hour. If it expires, request a new one by repeating the steps above.

Account and Login Help > Password and Login Issues
### I'm not receiving the password reset email
First, check your spam or junk folder. If it's not there:
- Make sure you're using the email address associated with your Stratify Labs account
- Try adding no-reply@stratifylabs.io to your contacts and request again
- If your company uses email filtering, ask your IT admin to allowlist mail from stratifylabs.io

Still nothing? Contact support@stratifylabs.io and we'll reset it for you manually.

Account and Login Help > Password and Login Issues
### My account is locked — what do I do?
Accounts are temporarily locked after several failed login attempts. To unlock your account:

1. Wait 15 minutes and try again — the lockout lifts automatically
2. If you're still locked out, click "Forgot password?" to reset your password, which also unlocks the account
3. If neither works, contact support@stratifylabs.io and we'll unlock your account right away

Account and Login Help > Password and Login Issues
### I can't log in with SSO — what should I check?
SSO login issues are usually caused by one of these:

1. **SSO not configured** — SSO is available on Professional and Enterprise plans. If your plan doesn't include it, you'll need to use email/password login.
2. **Identity provider misconfiguration** — Your IT admin may need to verify the SAML/OIDC setup in your IdP settings.
3. **Account not provisioned** — Your email address may not be in the IdP user directory. Ask your admin to add you.
4. **SSO enforced on your org** — If your org has enforced SSO and disabled password login, you must log in through your company's identity provider.

If you're the org Owner and have locked yourself out of SSO, contact support@stratifylabs.io — we have a recovery path that doesn't require going through your IdP.

Account and Login Help > Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
### How do I set up MFA?
1. Go to **Settings > Security > Authentication**
2. Click "Enable MFA"
3. Choose your preferred method: authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy), SMS, or hardware key (YubiKey, FIDO2)
4. Follow the setup instructions and enter the verification code to confirm

Authenticator apps and hardware keys are more secure than SMS and recommended for Owners and Admins.

Account and Login Help > Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
### I lost access to my MFA device — how do I recover?
If you set up backup codes when you enabled MFA, use one of those to log in:
1. On the MFA prompt, click "Use a recovery code"
2. Enter one of your backup codes
3. Once logged in, go to **Settings > Security** and reconfigure MFA with your new device

**No backup codes?** Contact support@stratifylabs.io from the email address on your account. We'll verify your identity and help you regain access. This process may take up to 1 business day for security reasons.

Account and Login Help > Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
### My organization requires MFA but I can't complete setup
If your org admin has enforced MFA, you'll be prompted to set it up on your next login before you can access anything else. If you're stuck in the MFA setup flow, contact support@stratifylabs.io with your account email and we'll assist.

Account and Login Help > Account Settings
### How do I change my email address?
1. Log in and go to **Settings > Profile**
2. Click "Change Email"
3. Enter your new email address
4. A verification link will be sent to the new address — click it to confirm the change

Your old email address continues to work until you verify the new one.

Account and Login Help > Account Settings
### How do I change my account name or display name?
Go to **Settings > Profile** and update your name. Changes take effect immediately.

Account and Login Help > Account Settings
### How do I delete my account?
Before deleting your account, note that:
- All your data, API keys, and settings will be permanently removed
- If you're the Organization Owner, you must transfer ownership to another member first (or delete the entire organization)
- Deletion cannot be undone

To delete your account, go to **Settings > Profile > Delete Account**. You'll be asked to confirm with your password.

If you're having trouble deleting your account, or if you're the last member of an organization and want to close everything, contact support@stratifylabs.io and we'll walk you through it.

Account and Login Help > Team Invitations
### I can't accept my team invitation — what should I do?
Invitation links expire after **7 days**. If your link has expired:
1. Ask your team's Owner or Admin to resend the invitation from **Settings > Team**
2. Check that you're opening the link in the same browser where you're not already logged in with a different account

If the link is still fresh and not working:
- Try opening it in an incognito/private browser window
- Make sure the email address on the invitation matches the one you're trying to sign up with

If you're still blocked, forward the invitation email to support@stratifylabs.io and we'll sort it out.

Account and Login Help > Team Invitations
### I sent a team invitation but the person never received it
Ask them to check their spam folder for an email from no-reply@stratifylabs.io. If it's not there, you can resend the invitation from **Settings > Team** — click the three-dot menu next to the pending invite and select "Resend."

Account and Login Help > Team Invitations
### How do I remove a team member?
Go to **Settings > Team**, find the member you want to remove, click the three-dot menu, and select "Remove." Their access is revoked immediately and their personal API keys are deactivated. Organization-level API keys are not affected.

Account and Login Help > Still Need Help?
If you're locked out and can't access your settings at all, email support@stratifylabs.io directly. Include:
- The email address on your account
- A brief description of what you're experiencing
- Whether your organization uses SSO

We'll get back to you as quickly as possible.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Understanding How Answers Are Built
### How does Stratify Labs produce an answer?
Every answer goes through two steps, often called RAG (retrieval-augmented generation):

1. **Retrieval** — your question is turned into a vector and compared with every chunk in the collection. The `top_k` most similar chunks are selected.
2. **Generation** — those chunks and your question are sent to the answer model, which is instructed to answer **only** from the provided content and cite its sources.

When an answer is wrong, the cause is almost always in one of these two steps. Check retrieval first: if the right content never reached the model, no amount of prompt tuning will fix the answer.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Understanding How Answers Are Built
### How do I tell if a bad answer is a retrieval problem or a generation problem?
Look at the `sources` in the response (or the **Sources** panel in the dashboard):

- **The right document isn't in the sources** → retrieval problem. Check that the content exists, check chunking, and try rephrasing.
- **The right document is in the sources but the answer is still wrong** → generation problem. Check temperature, the custom instructions, and whether the chunk contains the complete answer or only part of it.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Hallucinations
### The AI made up an answer that isn't in our documents — why?
Common causes:
1. **High temperature** — values above 0.7 make answers more creative and less faithful to the source. Use 0.0–0.3 for support content.
2. **Low confidence threshold** — weakly related chunks are being passed to the model, and it tries to stitch an answer together from them.
3. **Custom instructions that encourage guessing** — phrases like "always give the customer an answer" override the grounding rules.
4. **Partial content** — the chunk mentions a topic but not the specific answer, so the model fills the gap.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Hallucinations
### How do I reduce hallucinations?
- Keep temperature at **0.0–0.3**
- Raise the **confidence threshold** so weak matches are dropped (see below)
- Enable **Strict Grounding** at **Collections > Settings > Answer Behavior**. The model must cite a source for every claim, and answers without citations are replaced by your fallback message.
- Write a clear fallback message, such as "I couldn't find that in our help center — here's how to reach a person."

Answer Quality and Tuning > Tuning Retrieval
### What is the confidence threshold and how do I set it?
Every retrieved chunk has a relevance score from 0 to 1. Chunks below the confidence threshold are discarded before generation. If nothing passes, the user gets your fallback message instead of a guess.

- **Too high** (e.g., 0.90): the system says "I don't know" even when the answer exists.
- **Too low** (e.g., 0.40): irrelevant content gets through and answers drift off-topic.

Start at **0.70**, then adjust using the **Retrieval Debugger** at **Collections > Debug**, which shows every chunk's score for a test question.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Tuning Retrieval
### What chunk size should I use?
Chunk size controls how much text goes into each searchable piece.

| Content type | Recommended chunk size |
|--------------|-----------------------|
| FAQs and short Q&A | 300–500 characters |
| How-to guides and runbooks | 800–1,200 characters |
| Long policy or legal documents | 1,200–2,000 characters |

Chunks that are too small lose context (the answer gets split from its question). Chunks that are too large mix several topics, which lowers relevance scores. Changing chunk size requires re-indexing the collection.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Tuning Retrieval
### What is hybrid search?
Hybrid search combines semantic (meaning-based) search with keyword search. It helps when users search for exact terms that semantic search can miss, such as error codes (`ERR_4012`), product SKUs, or API parameter names. Enable it at **Collections > Settings > Search Mode > Hybrid** (Professional and Enterprise).

Answer Quality and Tuning > Tuning Retrieval
### What is reranking?
Reranking takes the top 20–50 retrieved chunks and re-scores them with a more precise model before choosing the final `top_k`. It typically improves answer accuracy by 10–20% on large or messy collections, at the cost of about 150 ms extra latency. Available on Professional and Enterprise.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Measuring Quality
### How do I know if our answers are getting better or worse?
Use three signals:
1. **User feedback** — thumbs up/down on answers, shown at **Analytics > Answer Feedback**
2. **"I don't know" rate** — the share of questions that hit the fallback message. A sudden jump often means content was deleted or a sync broke.
3. **An evaluation set** — 30 to 100 real questions with known correct answers. Run it at **Collections > Evaluate** after every major content or settings change and compare the score with the last run.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Measuring Quality
### How do I find gaps in our knowledge base?
Go to **Analytics > Unanswered Questions**. It groups questions that hit the fallback message by topic, sorted by volume. These are the articles you should write next. Many teams review this list weekly.

Answer Quality and Tuning > Measuring Quality
### Can I customize the tone and format of answers?
Yes. Add **Custom Instructions** at **Collections > Settings > Answer Behavior** — for example, "Use a friendly tone, keep answers under 120 words, and use numbered steps for procedures." Custom instructions change style only. They cannot override the grounding rules, and the model will still refuse to answer from outside your content.

API Reference Guide > Basics
### What is the base URL for the Stratify Labs API?
All API requests go to:

`https://api.stratifylabs.io/v1/{org}/`

Replace `{org}` with your organization's slug, which you chose during signup. You can find it at **Settings > Organization**. EU-West customers use `https://eu.api.stratifylabs.io/v1/{org}/` instead — sending EU data to the US endpoint returns a **421 Misdirected Request** error.

API Reference Guide > Basics
### How do I authenticate API requests?
Pass your API key in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer ak_live_yourkey
```

Never send the key as a query parameter — keys in URLs end up in proxy and server logs. Requests without a valid key return **401 Unauthorized**.

API Reference Guide > Basics
### Which API version should I use?
The current version is **v1**. We never make breaking changes inside a version. New optional fields and endpoints can be added at any time, so make sure your client ignores fields it doesn't recognize. When v2 ships, v1 will be supported for at least **12 months** after the v2 release date.

API Reference Guide > Core Endpoints
### What are the main endpoints?
| Method | Endpoint | What it does |
|--------|----------|--------------|
| POST | `/query` | Ask a question and get an AI answer with sources |
| POST | `/search` | Return matching chunks only — no AI-generated answer |
| POST | `/collections/{name}/documents` | Upload or update a document |
| GET | `/collections/{name}/documents/{id}` | Get a document and its ingestion status |
| DELETE | `/collections/{name}/documents/{id}` | Delete a document and its embeddings |
| GET | `/collections` | List collections |
| GET | `/usage` | Current usage against your plan limits |

API Reference Guide > Core Endpoints
### How do I send a query?
Send a POST to `/query` with a JSON body:

```json
{
  "collection": "support-articles",
  "question": "How do I reset my password?",
  "top_k": 5,
  "stream": false
}
```

The response includes the `answer`, a `sources` list (document ID, title, and relevance score for each chunk used), `usage` (tokens consumed), and a `request_id`.

API Reference Guide > Core Endpoints
### What's the difference between /query and /search?
- **/query** retrieves the most relevant chunks and then generates a natural-language answer from them. It counts as 1 API request plus generation tokens.
- **/search** only returns the matching chunks and their scores. It is faster (typically under 300ms) and cheaper, and is the right choice if you want to build your own answer UI or run your own LLM.

API Reference Guide > Core Endpoints
### Can I stream answers?
Yes. Set `"stream": true` in your `/query` request. The API returns Server-Sent Events (SSE): one `token` event per piece of text, then a final `done` event containing sources and usage. Streaming doesn't make the full answer finish sooner, but users see the first words in under a second, which makes the experience feel much faster.

API Reference Guide > Pagination, Request IDs and Idempotency
### How does pagination work?
List endpoints return up to 50 items by default (maximum 200, set with `limit`). If more results exist, the response includes a `next_cursor` value. Pass it as `cursor` on your next request. Cursors expire after 24 hours.

API Reference Guide > Pagination, Request IDs and Idempotency
### What is a request ID and why does support ask for it?
Every response includes an `X-Request-Id` header (for example, `req_8f2a1c9e`). It uniquely identifies that request in our logs. When you contact support about a failed or slow request, include the request ID and timestamp — it lets us find the exact request in seconds instead of searching by time window.

API Reference Guide > Pagination, Request IDs and Idempotency
### How do I avoid creating duplicate documents when I retry?
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (any unique string, such as a UUID) with POST requests. If you retry with the same key within 24 hours, we return the original response instead of processing the request again. This is especially important for document uploads in retry loops.

API Reference Guide > Errors
### Which errors should my code retry?
| Status | Retry? | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| 400 Bad Request | No | Fix the request body first |
| 401 / 403 | No | Key or permission problem |
| 404 Not Found | No | Check the collection name and document ID |
| 409 Conflict | No | Document is still processing; wait, then send the update |
| 413 Payload Too Large | No | File exceeds your plan's size limit |
| 429 Too Many Requests | Yes | Wait for the `Retry-After` seconds |
| 500 / 502 / 503 / 504 | Yes | Use exponential backoff with jitter |

For retryable errors, wait 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s (plus a random 0–1s of jitter) and stop after 5 attempts. Retrying immediately in a tight loop makes rate limiting worse and can extend an outage for everyone on your account.

API Reference Guide > SDKs and Timeouts
### Are there official SDKs?
Yes:
- **Python**: `pip install stratifylabs`
- **Node.js / TypeScript**: `npm install @stratifylabs/sdk`

Both SDKs handle authentication, retries with backoff, pagination, and streaming for you. Community libraries exist for Go and Ruby but are not officially supported.

API Reference Guide > SDKs and Timeouts
### What timeout should I set on my client?
We recommend:
- **/search**: 10 seconds
- **/query** (non-streaming): 30 seconds
- **/query** (streaming): 30 seconds to the first token, then no overall limit
- **Document uploads**: 60 seconds

The server-side limit for a single request is 60 seconds. Requests that run longer are cancelled and return **504 Gateway Timeout**.

Billing and Plans > Choosing the Right Plan
### Which plan is right for me?
Here's a quick breakdown to help you decide:

- **Free Trial** — Best if you're just exploring. 14 days, no credit card needed. Limited to 1,000 API requests/day and 1 collection.
- **Starter ($49/month)** — Good for small teams or early-stage products. 50,000 API requests/day, 5 collections, email support.
- **Professional ($199/month)** — For growing teams that need more scale, SSO, the EU-West data region option, and faster support response. 500,000 API requests/day, unlimited collections.
- **Enterprise (custom pricing)** — For large organizations with compliance requirements, dedicated infrastructure, or high-volume needs. Includes SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA options, and a dedicated support engineer.

Not sure? Email us at support@stratifylabs.io and we'll help you pick the right fit.

Billing and Plans > Choosing the Right Plan
### What's the difference between Starter and Professional?
Professional has 10x the daily request volume, unlimited collections, faster support, and the security and search features growing teams need:

| | Starter | Professional |
|--|---------|-------------|
| Price | $49/month ($470/year) | $199/month ($1,910/year) |
| Requests per minute / per day | 60 / 50,000 | 300 / 500,000 |
| Concurrent connections | 10 | 50 |
| Collections | 5 | Unlimited |
| Documents per collection | 50,000 | 500,000 |
| Max file size | 25 MB | 100 MB |
| Support | Email; Sev 1 first response in 24 hours | Priority email and live chat; Sev 1 first response in 2 hours |
| Uptime SLA | 99.5% | 99.9% |
| SSO (SAML 2.0 / OIDC) and IP allowlist | No | Yes |
| EU-West (Ireland) data region | No | Yes |
| Hybrid search, reranking, Answer Cache | No | Yes |
| Confluence Permission Sync | No | Yes |
| Integrations | 1 Slack workspace, 1 Zendesk instance, 5 Confluence spaces, 3 webhooks | 3 Slack workspaces, 2 Zendesk instances, 25 Confluence spaces, 10 webhooks |
| Sync frequency | Every 30 minutes | Every 15 minutes |

Enterprise adds custom limits, a 99.99% SLA, HIPAA configurations (with a signed BAA), custom roles, audit-log streaming to your SIEM, a dedicated support engineer, and a Technical Account Manager.

To switch, go to **Settings > Billing > Change Plan**. Upgrades take effect immediately.

Billing and Plans > Choosing the Right Plan
### What's included in the Free Trial?
The free trial is 14 days with no credit card required. You get:
- 1,000 API requests/day
- 1 collection (up to 10,000 documents)
- Community support

Your data is retained for 30 days after the trial ends. After that, it's permanently deleted unless you've upgraded to a paid plan.

Billing and Plans > Choosing the Right Plan
### Is there annual billing? Can I save money?
Yes. Annual billing is available for Starter and Professional plans at a 20% discount:
- **Starter Annual**: $470/year (saves $118 vs. monthly)
- **Professional Annual**: $1,910/year (saves $478 vs. monthly)

To switch to annual billing, go to **Settings > Billing** and select "Switch to Annual."

Billing and Plans > Understanding Your Bill
### What does my monthly charge include?
Your invoice has two parts:

1. **Base subscription** — the flat monthly fee for your plan
2. **Usage-based charges** — anything you use beyond your plan's included limits

Usage charges by plan:

| Resource | Starter | Professional | Enterprise |
|----------|---------|-------------|------------|
| Extra API requests | $0.002/request | $0.001/request | Custom |
| Extra storage | $0.10/GB/month | $0.05/GB/month | Custom |
| Embedding generation | $0.0001/document | $0.00005/document | Custom |
| Priority processing | Not available | $0.005/request | Included |

Usage charges are calculated daily and added to your monthly invoice.

Billing and Plans > Understanding Your Bill
### Where can I find my invoice?
Go to **Settings > Billing > Invoice History**. Invoices are also emailed to the billing address on your account on your billing date each month.

Each invoice shows:
- Base subscription cost
- Usage-based charges by resource type
- Applicable taxes
- Any credits or adjustments

Billing and Plans > Understanding Your Bill
### How do I update my billing email or payment method?
Go to **Settings > Billing** to update your payment method or billing contact email. We accept:
- Credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express)
- ACH bank transfers (US only — Starter and above)
- Wire transfers (Enterprise, minimum $1,000)
- Purchase orders (Enterprise only, NET 30 terms)

Billing and Plans > Understanding Your Bill
### I was charged unexpectedly — what happened?
Unexpected charges are usually caused by one of these:

1. **Usage overage** — You exceeded your plan's included API requests, storage, or document limit. Check **Settings > Billing > Usage** to see your usage breakdown.
2. **Annual renewal** — If you're on an annual plan, you were charged the full year upfront on your renewal date.
3. **Plan upgrade proration** — When you upgrade mid-cycle, you're charged a prorated amount for the remainder of the billing period.

If none of these explain the charge, contact support@stratifylabs.io with your invoice number and we'll look into it right away.

Billing and Plans > Understanding Your Bill
### How do I set up usage alerts to avoid surprise charges?
Go to **Settings > Billing > Alerts** and set thresholds at 50%, 75%, and 90% of your included limits. We'll email you when you approach those thresholds.

Billing and Plans > Upgrading and Downgrading
### How do I upgrade my plan?
Go to **Settings > Billing > Change Plan** and select the plan you want. Upgrades take effect immediately — you'll have access to higher limits and features right away. You'll be charged a prorated amount for the remainder of your current billing cycle.

Billing and Plans > Upgrading and Downgrading
### How do I downgrade my plan?
Go to **Settings > Billing > Change Plan** and select the lower tier. Downgrades take effect at the start of your next billing cycle — you keep current features until then.

**Important:** If your usage exceeds the lower tier's limits (for example, you have 8 collections but the Starter plan allows 5), you'll need to reduce your usage before the downgrade kicks in. Otherwise the system will block the downgrade until you're within limits.

Billing and Plans > Upgrading and Downgrading
### What happens to my data if I downgrade?
Your data is safe. The downgrade only affects your limits going forward. You won't lose documents unless your collections or document count exceeds what the new plan allows — in that case, you'll be prompted to reduce usage before the change takes effect.

Billing and Plans > Cancellation and Refunds
### How do I cancel my subscription?
You can cancel anytime at **Settings > Billing > Cancel Subscription**. There are no cancellation fees. After you cancel:

- Your data is retained for **30 days** — you can export everything during this window
- Your API keys are deactivated immediately
- After 30 days, all data is permanently and irreversibly deleted

If you change your mind within the 30-day window, contact support@stratifylabs.io and we can reactivate your account.

Billing and Plans > Cancellation and Refunds
### Can I get a refund?
- **New customers**: Full refund within 7 days of your first subscription (one-time, for first-time customers only).
- **Service outages**: If monthly uptime falls below your plan's SLA, you get a service credit of 10%, 25%, or 50% of the monthly fee, depending on how far below. Request it from billing@stratifylabs.io within 30 days of the end of the affected month.
- **Usage charges**: No refunds for API requests, storage, or processing already consumed.
- **Enterprise customers**: Refund terms are defined in your service agreement.

To request a refund, email support@stratifylabs.io with your account name and invoice number. We'll get back to you within 1 business day.

Billing and Plans > Cancellation and Refunds
### How do I export my data before canceling?
Go to **Settings > Security > Data Export** to download all your organization's data in JSON format. We recommend doing this before your account is fully cancelled — exported data includes your documents, collections, and metadata.

Billing and Plans > Taxes
### Do prices include taxes?
No — listed prices are exclusive of taxes. Applicable taxes (sales tax, VAT, GST) are calculated based on your billing address and added to your invoice.

To apply a tax exemption, upload your certificate at **Settings > Billing > Tax Info**.

EU customers: VAT is applied based on your country of residence. If you have a valid VAT ID, add it to your billing settings to apply the reverse charge mechanism.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Limits and Formats
### What are the file size and document limits?
| Limit | Free Trial | Starter | Professional | Enterprise |
|-------|-----------|---------|-------------|------------|
| Max file size | 10 MB | 25 MB | 100 MB | 500 MB |
| Documents per collection | 10,000 | 50,000 | 500,000 | Custom |
| Collections | 1 | 5 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Files per bulk upload | 50 | 200 | 1,000 | Custom |

Files over your plan's size limit are rejected with **413 Payload Too Large**. Split large documents (for example, by chapter) before uploading.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Limits and Formats
### Which file types are supported?
Text (.txt), Markdown (.md), PDF (.pdf, text-based only), HTML (.html), and CSV (.csv). Text must be UTF-8 encoded. For CSV files, each row is indexed as a separate document, and the first row must be a header row.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Ingestion Status
### What do the document statuses mean?
| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Queued** | Upload received, waiting for a processing slot |
| **Processing** | Text is being extracted, chunked, and embedded |
| **Indexed** | Ready — the document is searchable |
| **Partially indexed** | Some pages or rows failed; the rest are searchable |
| **Failed** | Nothing was indexed; see the error message on the document |

You can check status in the dashboard or with `GET /collections/{name}/documents/{id}`. You can also subscribe to the `document.indexed` and `document.failed` webhook events instead of polling.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Ingestion Status
### My document has been stuck in "Queued" or "Processing" for a long time
Normal processing takes 1–2 minutes per document. Large bulk uploads are processed in order, so the last files in a batch of 1,000 can take 20–30 minutes.

1. Check **status.stratifylabs.io** for ingestion pipeline delays.
2. Check the collection's queue depth at **Collections > (your collection) > Activity**.
3. If a single document has been in **Processing** for more than 60 minutes while others finish, delete and re-upload it.

If it still doesn't complete, contact support@stratifylabs.io with the document ID.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Common Ingestion Errors
### My PDF failed with "No extractable text"
The PDF is a scanned image or a photo of a document, so there's no text layer to read. Run it through OCR software (most PDF editors have a "Recognize Text" option), save it, and upload again. To check, open the PDF and try to select a sentence — if you can't highlight the text, it needs OCR.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Common Ingestion Errors
### My PDF failed with "Document is encrypted"
Password-protected or permission-restricted PDFs can't be processed. Remove the password (File > Properties > Security in most PDF readers), save a new copy, and upload that.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Common Ingestion Errors
### I'm getting "Invalid encoding" errors on text or CSV files
The file isn't UTF-8. This is common with CSVs exported from older versions of Excel. Re-save the file as **CSV UTF-8** (Excel: File > Save As > CSV UTF-8), or convert it with a text editor that lets you choose the encoding.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Common Ingestion Errors
### My CSV was only partially indexed
Usually caused by rows with a different number of columns than the header — often from unescaped commas or line breaks inside a field. Wrap fields that contain commas or line breaks in double quotes. The document's error details list the first 20 failing row numbers.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Common Ingestion Errors
### Tables in my PDF come out jumbled in answers
PDF text extraction reads left to right, which can scramble multi-column layouts and complex tables. For table-heavy content, export the table as CSV or Markdown and upload it separately so each row stays intact.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Updating and Deleting
### How do I update a document that has changed?
Upload it again with the **same document ID** (`PUT /collections/{name}/documents/{id}`, or **Replace** in the dashboard). The old chunks and embeddings are removed and the new version is indexed. Uploading under a new ID creates a duplicate, and both versions will appear in search results.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Updating and Deleting
### Why am I seeing old content in answers after I updated a document?
1. **It was uploaded as a new document** instead of replacing the old one — search the collection for the old title and delete the outdated copy.
2. **Re-indexing hasn't finished** — the old version stays searchable until the new one reaches **Indexed**.
3. **Answer Cache** — if enabled, cached answers expire within 60 minutes, or you can clear the cache at **Collections > Settings > Performance**.
4. **Synced source not updated** — for Zendesk or Confluence, the change appears after the next sync.

Document Ingestion and Indexing > Updating and Deleting
### When I delete a document, is it removed immediately?

Stratify Labs is an AI-powered knowledge base platform. ### 2. How is Stratify Labs different from a regular search engine?
Traditional search engines match keywords. If you search for "can't log in" and your article says "account access issues," keyword search might miss it.

Stratify Labs uses semantic search — it understands that "can't log in" and "account access issues" are related concepts and returns the right content either way. It's also designed to pull the specific, relevant chunk of a document rather than returning the whole page.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Models We Use
### Which AI models power Stratify Labs?
Stratify Labs uses two kinds of models:

- **Answer models** generate the natural-language answer from your retrieved content. You can choose between **Fast** (lowest latency and cost, the default) and **Advanced** (better reasoning on complex, multi-step questions, roughly 3x the generation cost).
- **Embedding models** turn your documents and queries into vectors for semantic search. Every collection is tied to one embedding model version, shown at **Collections > (your collection) > Settings > Embedding Model**.

Enterprise customers can bring their own model (BYOM) — see the FAQ for details.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Models We Use
### How do I change the answer model?
Set it per collection at **Collections > Settings > Answer Model**, or per request by passing `"model": "advanced"` in the `/query` body. A per-request setting overrides the collection default. Changing the answer model does not require re-indexing.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Deprecation Policy
### How much notice do you give before retiring a model?
- **Answer models**: at least **90 days** notice before retirement.
- **Embedding models**: at least **6 months** notice, because switching requires re-indexing your content.

Notices go to the account Owner and all Admins by email, appear as a banner in the dashboard, and are listed at status.stratifylabs.io/deprecations. Enterprise customers are also contacted directly by their dedicated support engineer.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Deprecation Policy
### What happens on the retirement date if I haven't migrated?
For answer models, requests that name the retired model are automatically routed to its listed replacement, and the response includes a `X-Stratify-Model-Redirect` header so you can detect it. You will not get errors, but answers may read differently.

For embedding models, collections that haven't been re-indexed by the retirement date are switched to **read-only**: search keeps working on existing content, but new uploads fail with a **409 Conflict** error until you re-index.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Deprecation Policy
### What is model pinning?
Pinning locks a collection to a specific model version (for example, `fast-2026-03`) instead of the moving alias (`fast`). The alias is upgraded automatically when we release improvements; a pinned version is not. Pin a version if you have automated tests or compliance review that depend on consistent wording. Pinned versions are still subject to the deprecation policy above.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Migrating
### How do I re-index a collection onto a new embedding model?
1. Go to **Collections > (your collection) > Settings > Embedding Model**
2. Select the new model and click **Start Re-index**
3. A shadow copy of the index is built in the background. Search keeps using the old index until the new one is complete, so there is no downtime.
4. When it finishes, compare results in the **Preview** tab, then click **Promote**.

Re-indexing time depends on collection size — roughly 10 minutes per 10,000 documents. Embedding generation for re-indexing is billed at the normal per-document rate, except during the final 30 days before a forced retirement, when it is free.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Migrating
### Can I roll back after promoting a new embedding model?
Yes, for **7 days**. The previous index is kept and can be restored from **Collections > Settings > Index History**. After 7 days it is deleted.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Migrating
### Why can't I mix embedding models in one collection?
Vectors from different embedding models live in different mathematical spaces, so comparing them gives meaningless similarity scores. If a query is embedded with one model and documents with another, search returns confidently wrong results. This is why the whole collection must be re-indexed together.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Troubleshooting After a Model Change
### Answers changed after a model upgrade — is this a bug?
Usually not. New answer models can phrase things differently, give longer or shorter answers, or cite different chunks even with the same content. To check:

1. Look at the `model` field in the API response to confirm which version answered.
2. Compare the `sources` list from before and after. If the sources are the same and only the wording changed, it's the new model's style.
3. If you need the old behavior, pin the previous version while you adjust your prompts or tests.

If the sources themselves changed after an **embedding** migration, or answer quality dropped noticeably, contact support@stratifylabs.io with example queries and the before/after request IDs.

AI Models, Upgrades and Deprecations > Troubleshooting After a Model Change
### Search quality dropped right after re-indexing — what should I check?
1. **Confidence threshold** — new embedding models often produce scores on a different scale. A threshold tuned for the old model (for example, 0.80) may now filter out good results. Re-tune it using the Preview tab.
2. **Partial re-index** — check that the re-index status is "Complete" and the document count matches the old index.
3. **Custom integrations caching vectors** — if your own system stores query embeddings, it must switch to the new model at the same time.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > What Normal Looks Like
### How fast should Stratify Labs respond?
Typical latency for a collection under 100,000 documents, measured inside the same region:

| Endpoint | p50 (median) | p95 |
|----------|--------------|-----|
| `/search` | 150 ms | 400 ms |
| `/query` (first token, streaming) | 600 ms | 1.2 s |
| `/query` (full answer, non-streaming) | 2.0 s | 4.5 s |
| Document upload accepted | 200 ms | 500 ms |

Most of a `/query` request's time is spent generating the answer, not searching. That's why streaming makes the biggest difference to how fast your app feels.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > What Normal Looks Like
### What do p50 and p95 mean?
- **p50 (median)**: half of requests are faster than this.
- **p95**: 95% of requests are faster than this; 1 in 20 is slower.

Averages hide slow outliers, so we report percentiles. If your p95 is much higher than the numbers above, some of your users are having a slow experience even if the average looks fine.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > What Normal Looks Like
### How can I see where the time is going?
Every `/query` response includes timing headers:
- `X-Stratify-Retrieval-Ms` — time spent embedding the query and searching
- `X-Stratify-Generation-Ms` — time spent generating the answer
- `X-Stratify-Queue-Ms` — time the request waited because you were at your concurrency limit

If `Queue-Ms` is high, you're hitting your concurrent connection limit. If `Retrieval-Ms` is high, look at collection size and `top_k`. If `Generation-Ms` is high, look at answer length and model choice.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > Making It Faster
### What are the quickest ways to reduce latency?
1. **Stream answers** (`"stream": true`) so users see text in under a second.
2. **Use /search instead of /query** when you don't need an AI-written answer.
3. **Query a specific collection** rather than searching across all of them.
4. **Keep top_k small** — 3 to 5 chunks is usually enough. Each extra chunk adds input tokens and generation time.
5. **Use the Fast answer model** unless you need Advanced reasoning.
6. **Reuse HTTP connections** — create one API client and reuse it. Opening a new TLS connection for every request adds 100–300 ms.
7. **Deploy close to your data region** — calling US-East from Asia adds 150–250 ms per round trip.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > Making It Faster
### Should I cache answers?
For high-traffic, repeated questions (like "How do I reset my password?"), yes. Cache responses for a short window (5–60 minutes) keyed on the normalized question and collection. Clear the cache when you update the underlying documents, or you'll serve stale answers. Professional and Enterprise plans can enable **Answer Cache** at **Collections > Settings > Performance**, which does this automatically and invalidates on document updates.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > Making It Faster
### Why is the first request after a quiet period slower?
Collections that haven't been queried for over 24 hours are moved to warm storage. The first query after that may take 1–3 extra seconds while the index is loaded into memory. Enterprise customers can enable **Always Warm** to keep indexes in memory permanently.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > Timeouts and Retries
### My requests are timing out — what should I check?
1. **Your client timeout** — make sure it's at least 30 seconds for non-streaming `/query`. A 5-second timeout will cut off normal long answers.
2. **Very large prompts** — a high `top_k` combined with large chunks can push requests near the model's context limit, which slows generation sharply.
3. **status.stratifylabs.io** — check for an active incident.
4. **Your network** — corporate proxies sometimes buffer or terminate streaming responses. Test from outside the proxy.

If timeouts continue, send the request IDs to support@stratifylabs.io.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > Timeouts and Retries
### How should I retry failed requests?
Use **exponential backoff with jitter**: wait 1s, then 2s, 4s, 8s, adding a random 0–1 second each time, and give up after 5 attempts. Only retry 429 and 5xx errors. Always honor the `Retry-After` header on 429 responses.

Avoid retrying without delays — when many clients retry at the same moment, they create a "thundering herd" that can turn a brief blip into a longer outage.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > Timeouts and Retries
### What is a circuit breaker and do I need one?
A circuit breaker stops sending requests to a service after repeated failures (for example, 5 failures in 30 seconds), returns a fallback immediately, and then tests again after a cool-down period. It protects your app from hanging on a struggling dependency. For customer-facing chat, a good fallback is a friendly "Search is temporarily unavailable — here's how to contact support" message.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > Concurrency and Load
### What happens if I go over my concurrent connection limit?
Requests over the limit are queued for up to 10 seconds (shown in `X-Stratify-Queue-Ms`). If a slot doesn't open in that time, the request fails with **429 Too Many Requests** and code `concurrency_limit_exceeded`. Concurrent connection limits are 2 (Free Trial), 10 (Starter), 50 (Professional), and custom for Enterprise.

Performance, Latency and Reliability > Concurrency and Load
### We're planning a launch — how do we prepare for a traffic spike?
1. Load-test against a **test key** (`ak_test_`) in the sandbox first — test traffic doesn't count toward your limits.
2. Estimate your peak requests per minute and confirm it's within your plan's limit with headroom.
3. Enable answer caching for your most common questions.
4. Enterprise customers: tell your TAM at least **5 business days** before the launch so we can pre-scale capacity and keep an engineer on standby.

### What can I use Stratify Labs for?
Stratify Labs answers questions from your own content. The three most common uses:

- **Customer-facing chatbot or help widget** — answers customers from your public help articles, around the clock.
- **Internal knowledge assistant** — answers employees from wikis, runbooks, HR policies, and engineering specs, in Slack or your own tools.
- **Agent Assist in Zendesk** — shows support agents the top 3 relevant answers in the ticket sidebar, ready to insert into a reply.

Product Overview and Core Concepts > What Stratify Labs Does
### How does Stratify Labs work?
1. **You add documents to a collection**: upload files, send them through the API, or sync them from Zendesk or Confluence.
2. **Each document is split into chunks**, and each chunk is turned into an embedding (a vector that captures its meaning).
3. **Someone asks a question.** Retrieval compares the question with every chunk in the collection and picks the `top_k` most relevant ones (semantic search, or hybrid search on Professional and Enterprise).
4. **The answer model writes the answer only from those chunks** and returns it with its sources. You can choose the Fast model (default) or the Advanced model.
5. **If no chunk passes the confidence threshold**, the user gets your fallback message instead of a guess.

Product Overview and Core Concepts > Core Concepts
### What is a collection?
A collection is a named group of documents that is searched together, such as `customer-help`, `agent-internal`, or `engineering-runbooks`. You name the collection in each query; querying one specific collection is faster than searching across all of them.

- **Group collections by who searches them**, not by where the content came from. Mixing internal and customer-facing content in one collection risks internal notes appearing in customer answers.
- **Each collection has its own settings**: answer model, confidence threshold, search mode, chunk size, Answer Cache, and Custom Instructions, all under **Collections > Settings**.
- **Each collection is tied to one embedding model.** Switching models means re-indexing the whole collection.
- **Collection names are case-sensitive** in the API. A wrong case returns 404.
- **Limits by plan**: Free Trial 1 collection, Starter 5, Professional and Enterprise unlimited.

Product Overview and Core Concepts > Core Concepts
### What is a document?
A document is one item in a collection: a .txt, .md, .pdf (text-based), or .html file, one row of a CSV file, or a synced Zendesk article, ticket, or macro, or Confluence page. Every document has an ID. To update a document, upload the new version with the same ID; a new ID creates a duplicate. You can attach up to 20 metadata fields per document and filter searches by them.

A document moves through **Queued → Processing → Indexed**. It is searchable once it reaches Indexed, usually within 1–2 minutes.

Product Overview and Core Concepts > Core Concepts
### What are chunks, embeddings, and sources?
- **Chunk**: a searchable piece of a document. Chunk size is set per collection (300–500 characters suits FAQs; 800–1,200 suits how-to guides).
- **Embedding**: a list of numbers that represents a chunk's meaning, created by the collection's embedding model. Questions are embedded the same way, and the closest chunks are retrieved.
- **Sources**: the chunks used to write an answer, returned in the `sources` list with each document's ID, title, and relevance score. When an answer looks wrong, check the sources first.

Product Overview and Core Concepts > Core Concepts
### What are top_k and the confidence threshold?
- **top_k** is how many chunks are sent to the answer model. 3 to 5 is usually enough; more adds latency and cost.
- **Confidence threshold** is the minimum relevance score (0 to 1) a chunk needs to be used. Start at **0.70** and tune it in the Retrieval Debugger at **Collections > Debug**.

### I'm getting a 401 Unauthorized error
A **401** means your API key is missing, invalid, or has been revoked.

**What to check:**
1. **Is the key in the request?** Make sure you're passing the key in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer ak_live_yourkey`.
2. **Is the key still active?** Go to Settings > API Keys to check. The key may have been rotated or deleted.
3. **Was the key found in a public repo?** If we detect your key in a public GitHub repository, we automatically revoke it and send an email to the account owner. Check your inbox.
4. **Right key for the right environment?** Test keys (`ak_test_`) only work against the sandbox. Live keys (`ak_live_`) are required for production.

If you've verified all of the above and still get 401s, generate a new key from Settings > API Keys and test with that.

**Common causes:**
- You're using a read-only key (`ak_readonly_`) to make a write request
- Your role doesn't have access to the collection or resource you're querying

2. **Organization name** — if your API endpoint includes your org name, verify it matches exactly.

### My API responses are slow — what could be causing this?
Slow responses can have a few causes:

1. **Large knowledge base** — searching across many documents takes longer. Make sure you're querying a specific collection rather than searching everything.
2. **First query after ingestion** — the first query after adding new documents may take 2–5 seconds while embeddings are generated. This is normal; subsequent queries will be faster.
3. **High concurrency** — if you're approaching your concurrent connection limit, requests may queue. Check your plan's concurrent connection limit and consider upgrading if needed.
4. **Network latency** — if your application is in a different region from your Stratify Labs data region, there will be added latency. Enterprise plans support multi-region deployment.
5. **Large result sets** — requesting a high `top_k` value (many results per query) increases processing time. Start with 5 and increase only if needed.

If your latency is consistently above the normal range (p95 of 400 ms for `/search` or 4.5 seconds for a full non-streaming `/query` answer, see Performance and Latency) and none of the above applies, contact support@stratifylabs.io with the request IDs of slow requests.

Troubleshooting Common Errors > Knowledge Base and Search Issues
### My embeddings aren't updating after I ingest new documents
After ingestion, embeddings are generated in the background. This usually takes 1–2 minutes for normal-sized documents. Large documents or large batches can take longer.

**What to check:**
1. **Wait a bit longer** — give it 5 minutes, then try your query again.
2. **Verify the document ingested** — check your collection in the dashboard to confirm the document appears. If it doesn't show up, the ingestion may have failed.
3. **Check for ingestion errors** — go to your collection and look for any error indicators on recently uploaded documents.

If a document shows as ingested but still isn't returning in search results after 10 minutes, contact support@stratifylabs.io.

Troubleshooting Common Errors > Knowledge Base and Search Issues
### My query is returning wrong or irrelevant answers
If the answers you're getting back don't match what you asked, here are the most common reasons:

1. **Your knowledge base doesn't contain relevant content** — the system can only return what's in your documents. If the right answer isn't in your KB, it won't appear. Check whether the relevant content has been ingested.
2. **Query is too vague** — more specific queries return more relevant results. Try rephrasing your question to be more precise.
3. **Confidence threshold is too low** — if your app is set to return low-confidence results, you'll see less relevant content. Raise the confidence threshold in your collection settings.
4. **Chunk size mismatch** — if documents were chunked in a way that splits key context, results may seem incomplete. Check your collection's chunking settings.
5. **Wrong collection** — make sure you're querying the collection that contains the relevant documents.

If you've checked all of the above and are still seeing consistently poor results, contact support@stratifylabs.io with example queries and expected vs. actual answers. We can help tune the configuration.

### Why does the AI say "I don't know" or give no answer?
This means no content in your knowledge base met the confidence threshold for your query. It's actually the correct behavior — the system is designed not to make up answers.

To improve coverage:
- Add more relevant documents to your knowledge base
- Make sure documents are properly formatted and not truncated
- Try rewriting the query to match the language used in your documents
